The ISM dose is one 25 mg tablet a day (openFDA label 645c887c, section 2.4) and the 25 mg NDC 72064-125-30 is a 30-tablet bottle (openFDA NDC), so a bottle is 30 days: 42,838 x 365/30 = $521,195.67 a year. column12: Judgement on the comparator: Ayvakit is the only approved KIT D816V inhibitor for ISM, the product elenestinib is designed to succeed, same company, same prescribers, same payer channel (Part D and commercial specialty pharmacy), so a successor launches at or near its price. The WAC path is measured: $38,929 in January 2024 (Connecticut prescriber notice), $40,837 in January 2025 (ayvakit.com patient support page), $42,838 in January 2026, about 5% a year. The case for lower: generic avapritinib could arrive after the US compound patent (October 2034 per Sanofi FY2025 20-F) and pull the class price down. Cross-check against the CMS route: Part D 2025 spend per claim was $41,575.46 (6,034 claims, $250,866,345.29; quarterly file 4ff7c618, row 2025 (Q1-Q4)), within 2% of the 2025 WAC, so the list price is what Part D pays per fill. The house 0.5 on spend per beneficiary ($323,698.51 x 0.5 = $161,849) is not used: a launch still adding patients carries part-year beneficiaries (7.79 fills each in 2025), and the brief puts a published list price ahead of that basis

column11: Ayvakit's own discount, measured in two steps. First, Blueprint's FY2024 10-K (0001558370-25-000953, Note 6): provisions related to current-period sales of $80,847k against US net product revenue of $421,837k, so 80,847 / (421,837 + 80,847) = 16.08% off gross (17.00% in 2023 on $37,281k and $181,971k). Second, Sanofi's Q2 2026 release (6-K 0001121404-26-000008): higher US government rebates since Blueprint became part of Sanofi cost c.9 points of growth on Q2 2025's $175.1mm, $15.76mm, against Q2 2026 US sales of EUR 168mm, $195.68mm at the release's own pro forma rate of 221.3/190 = 1.1647. Without the extra rebates US net would be 195.68 + 15.76 = $211.43mm, a gross of 211.43 / (1 - 0.1608) = $251.96mm, so the discount now is 1 - 195.68/251.96 = 22.34%

Sanofi says the extra rebates continue, which is why the current rate is used rather than Blueprint's. column12: MULTIPLE 1.0, A JUDGEMENT: elenestinib is given the rate its predecessor achieved in the same pool. The case for lower: from late 2034 it may compete with generic avapritinib, which payers could require first; the non-advanced SM candidates Blueprint named as competitors (Cogent Biosciences, Alys, Celldex and others, FY2024 10-K) may be on the market by then; and a successor wins its early patients by switching, which this seed does not count
